aboutH2: Hidden Secret Recovery: Private Residential Addiction Treatment in Nauwigewauk, New Brunswick
intro: Hidden Secret Recovery is a small private addiction treatment centre on Darlings Island in Nauwigewauk, a few minutes from Hampton in Kings County. It runs a live-in program for adults working on alcohol or drug use, and it takes no more than eight people at a time. The program is housed in a restored private home on a gated property, so residents eat at a real dining table and sleep in ordinary bedrooms.

The standard stay is 30 days, and the centre adjusts the length to the person. Days follow a set routine of one-to-one counselling, group sessions, shared meals, wellness activities and some free time. The centre tests for drugs and alcohol throughout the stay, and it builds 12 step work and peer support into the program. Staff are on site around the clock.

pillars.title: A Restored Home on Darlings Island
pillars.body: The program runs in a fully restored private house on a gated property at 277 Darlings Island Road, near Hampton in Kings County. The grounds take in water, wetlands and mature trees, with stone walking paths through the woods. Inside there is a main room with a fireplace and tall windows, a shared kitchen, a dining area that looks out over the property and shared bedrooms. A detached garage has a games room and a movie theatre upstairs and a gym downstairs. The house holds eight people at most.

pillars.title: A Year of Aftercare Built In
pillars.body: Anyone who completes the live-in program or the outpatient service can stay in aftercare for one year. That means group support sessions, regular accountability and continued contact with the team. Before discharge, staff help plan what comes next, which might be outpatient counselling, peer support groups or a return to work. Families are not left out either: the centre runs a family support service with one-to-one guidance, education about addiction and practical help with communication and boundaries.

pillars.title: A Family Founded Centre With a Clinical Team
pillars.body: Adam Beman started Hidden Secret Recovery with his parents, Mike and Lisa Beman, after the family lived through Adam's own addiction. Adam is in recovery, works as a CanAm-certified interventionist and runs the centre as director. The clinical side includes Karen Thomas, a Registered Nurse who spent 15 years managing detox at Ridgewood in Saint John, and Charles Dufty, a Licensed Addiction Counsellor. They work alongside social work graduates, peer support workers and residential workers, and many of the residential staff are in recovery too.

overview: The clinical side includes a Registered Nurse, a Licensed Practical Nurse and Licensed Addiction Counsellors, along with social work graduates and a CanAm-certified interventionist. The centre also says it is an approved provider with the New Brunswick Department of Social Development. Many of the residential workers are in recovery themselves and say so on the centre's team page.

Not everyone needs to live in. Hidden Secret Recovery also offers outpatient counselling, delivered as one-to-one virtual sessions with flexible scheduling, and a support program for parents, partners and other family members. Anyone who finishes the live-in program or outpatient services can join a year of aftercare with group sessions and regular check-ins.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and its recovery.com profile. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Hidden Secret Recovery cost?
faqs.a: The standard 30-day residential program costs $11,500, as published on the centre's website. Financing through MediCard is available, with an example rate of about $214 a month over 72 months. Payment is private, so call the centre to go over your options.

faqs.q: Is Hidden Secret Recovery covered by Medicare or insurance?
faqs.a: No, it is a private centre and New Brunswick Medicare does not cover the program. The centre provides receipts for eligible services to plans such as Telus Health and Medavie Blue Cross, and some employer benefit plans and EAP programs may cover part of the cost. WorkSafeNB, NIHB and Social Development NB referrals are accepted in eligible or approved cases.

faqs.q: How long is the residential program?
faqs.a: The live-in program typically lasts 30 days. The centre says it adjusts the length to each person's needs. A year of aftercare follows the residential stay.

faqs.q: Does Hidden Secret Recovery offer detox?
faqs.a: The centre's website does not list a medical detox service, and its recovery.com profile lists detox as not offered. If you are still drinking or using heavily, ask the admissions team on the first call how withdrawal should be handled before you arrive.

faqs.q: Who works at Hidden Secret Recovery?
faqs.a: The team includes a Registered Nurse, a Practical Nurse, a Licensed Addiction Counsellor, social work graduates and a CanAm-certified interventionist. Staff are on site 24 hours a day. Many of the residential workers have their own lived experience of addiction and recovery.

faqs.q: How many people stay at the centre at once?
faqs.a: The centre takes a maximum of eight residents. It is a restored private home on a gated property on Darlings Island, with shared bedrooms, a shared kitchen and a dining room. A detached building holds a games room, a movie theatre and a gym.

faqs.q: Where is Hidden Secret Recovery and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 277 Darlings Island Road in Nauwigewauk, New Brunswick, near Hampton in Kings County. Saint John is about 30 minutes away by car, Sussex about 40 minutes, and Moncton and Fredericton each about an hour and a half. Call before you travel so the team can plan your arrival.
The centre says it has no waitlist and can usually arrange admission within days of first contact. Intake starts with a confidential conversation by phone at 506-607-0632.

faqs.q: Does Hidden Secret Recovery offer outpatient or virtual counselling?
faqs.a: Yes. Outpatient counselling is offered as one-to-one virtual sessions with flexible scheduling, for people who want to keep working or caring for family while they get help. Existing outpatient clients book through an online client portal.

Graduates get one year of aftercare, including group sessions, ongoing accountability and continued contact with the team. The centre also helps plan the next step, whether that is outpatient counselling, peer support or a return to work.

Yes. Family involvement is encouraged, and visits are arranged during intake. The centre also runs a separate family support service with one-to-one guidance, education on addiction and help with communication and boundaries.
